rules.statement: When an entity stores references to other records as a denormalized JSON array instead of a join table, validate on every create and update that each referenced value exists on the target owner, and reject the write if any is unknown.
rules.why: Write-time validation means no dangling reference is ever introduced, which is what makes a JSON array safe to use in place of a normalized join.
rules.check: Look for create/update paths that persist a JSON list of reference values (e.g. granted scopes) without first checking each value against the owning record's current set and returning a validation error for unknown values.

rules.statement: When reading a denormalized list of references, compute the effective set as its intersection with the referenced records that currently exist, so stale values are ignored rather than trusted or treated as errors.
rules.why: A later deletion can leave a stale value in the array. Intersecting at read time makes such a dangling reference harmless and removes any need to cascade or clean up on deletion.
rules.check: Look for code that uses stored reference values (e.g. a client grant's scopes) directly without intersecting them with the current scopes of the owning resource server, or that throws when it finds a stale value.

rules.statement: Treat a scope as owned by exactly one resource server (API), so its identity is the pair (resource server, value); never look up or match a scope by its value alone across resource servers.
rules.why: The same scope name can mean different things on different APIs, so the same value on two resource servers is two distinct scopes.
rules.check: Look for scope queries, uniqueness constraints or comparisons keyed only on the scope value without the owning resource server, and for scope catalogs shared across APIs.

rules.statement: Model the standard OIDC scopes (openid, profile, email, address, phone, offline_access) as system scopes under a reserved system resource server seeded per tenant, not as a separate special-case path, and reject deletion of any system resource server or system scope.
rules.why: This keeps one uniform model where every scope sits under a resource server, and the standard scopes must always be present.
rules.check: Look for hard-coded identity-scope handling that bypasses the resource server model, and for delete operations on resource servers or scopes that do not refuse rows marked IsSystem.

rules.statement: Enforce uniqueness of an operator-supplied identifier or value through a normalized companion column with a unique index scoped to its owner (such as tenant or parent entity), not by comparing the raw value.
rules.why: Values like a resource server identifier or a scope value must be unique per owner, and a normalized column is the consistent way to apply that constraint.
rules.check: Look for new entities with user-meaningful identifiers that lack a Normalized* column, a unique index scoped to the owner, or that check uniqueness on the raw value.

rules.statement: Make tenant-owned management entities and their child compositions tenant-scoped, so they are only materialized within the ambient tenant.
rules.why: Scopes, APIs and client grants are a tenant concern and must follow the tenant-scoped data access model.
rules.check: Look for new tenant-owned entities or child entities that lack TenantId or the tenant query filter, or for queries that bypass it.
